A_vee_pulley.title: The brief's configuration: bow-pulley V + 2 rear bumpers + 2 dockwheels
A_vee_pulley.note: Second-to-last of seventeen (section 15.2). One rope path, so the loss of any single element leaves no equilibrium in reverse. Sway is near-unrestrained: it fails 4 of 16 wind cases on demands of a few tens of newtons.

C_vee_legs_crossed.title: Smallest correction to the brief: fixed bow legs + 2 crossed stern ropes
C_vee_legs_crossed.note: Two ropes and no new fittings take the brief's layout from 2218 N / 1586 N / no redundancy to 600 N / 708 N / full redundancy.

I_fwd_midship_crossed.title: Recommended on mechanics (section 15): 2 midship springs + 2 crossed stern ropes
I_fwd_midship_crossed.note: Best of seventeen: 600 N preload, 647 N peak, full redundancy, holds all 16 wind cases. Conflicts with the cahier des charges under a broad reading of 'the boat carries nothing' (section 17).

X_yoke_midship_crossed.title: MEASURED NEGATIVE RESULT (section 19): arrangement I with the midship springs equalised into one rope
X_yoke_midship_crossed.note: Kept as evidence, not as an option. One winch and one tensioning action instead of four, at 3,5x the preload (2120 N) and 6,3x the peak load (4080 N), with a single point of failure and contact lost in a 0,3 m beam wave. A symmetric equalised pair has provably ZERO yaw capacity, and the binding case diff_opp is pure yaw: the springs' job is to be unequal. Also needs a powered winch, which arrangement I does not. Section 19 has the mechanism.

U_sling_midship.title: Under-hull slings (snug) + 2 midship springs carrying the preload
U_sling_midship.note: The slings halve the roll transmitted to the boat but cost a factor of 6 in peak rope load. Preloading them is a bad trade: +63 % peak load to buy 0.8 deg of roll (sling_preload.json).

V_spec_zero_fittings.title: Zero boat fittings: 2 under-hull slings + 2 bow legs on a stem saddle + bumpers + wheels
V_spec_zero_fittings.note: The only arrangement tested that satisfies the cahier des charges in full: everything bears on the hull, nothing attaches to it, so it can target 80 % of boats. Costs a factor of 6 in peak rope load and half the redundancy against arrangement I, and buys a factor of 3 in roll.

W_spec_sling_only.title: Slings + bumpers + wheels only, no surge element
W_spec_sling_only.note: FAILS the static gate, as the geometry predicts: a transverse sling has a surge direction cosine of exactly zero, so nothing restrains reverse. Kept as the negative control.

O_aft_breasts.title: 2 aft breast ropes to the stern cleats + bumpers + wheels
O_aft_breasts.note: Excellent in surge (0.92 direction cosine in half the bow leg's length, clean geometry) and useless in yaw: unrestrained under diff_opp. Half an arrangement.

G_six_rope_wheels.title: The 30 Oct six-rope arrangement, with the dockwheels added
G_six_rope_wheels.note: Full redundancy over six elements, but six tensioning actions to couple.

K_tubes_aft_vee.title: 2 aft tubes with elastomer cartridges + bow-pulley V + wheels
K_tubes_aft_vee.note: Lowest loads of any arrangement, but the brackets are a permanent modification.

stiffness_note: All three contact stiffnesses are UNMEASURED. They spread the quasi-static answer by a factor of 3, although rope tension pins the rear compression exactly (COUPLING.md section 7).

exo.note: per float row: ITTC-57 friction on the wetted area x (1+k) + Cd x submerged frontal area of one float for the nose/flat-end junctions and gaps (ASSUMED coefficients; the flat-to-flat junction of the rear and middle floats and the nose-to-flat junction of the middle and end floats are not resolved)

boat.note: ITTC-57 friction on the proxy hull's wetted area x (1+k) x appendages (keel, rudder, propeller) + residuary C_R = c (Fr/0.2)^n on the wetted area (ASSUMED; the proxy hull is not the real hull)

resistance_cfg.drag_points: EXO: resultant at the centroid of the submerged float volume (world); boat: at its centre of buoyancy

coefficients.note: ASSUMED first-harmonic wind coefficients for a bluff, partly open small-craft structure. Cx0 and Cy0 refer to the frontal and lateral projected areas, Cn0 to A_lateral x L. No wind-tunnel, CFD or full-scale basis. These three numbers are the largest single uncertainty in any wind result.

pose.warning: The coupled solve with thrust applied converges to a capsized branch (heel 88.6 deg) and reports itself physical. All figures here use the thrust-off pose (heel -0.00 deg). The project's forward-100 % resistance of 841 N was computed at the capsized pose and is understated by 37 %.
